entries.title: Entering the Allen School
body: I'm excited to share that I will be joining the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering at the University of Washington next quarter.
I will officially become a computer science student and continue building toward work in human-centered design and software development.

entries.title: Joining Thermo Fisher Scientific
body: I'm happy to share that I am joining Thermo Fisher Scientific as a Software Engineering Intern in Shanghai.
I will contribute to YOLO26-based vision for robot-assisted tube handling, 3500Dx localization testing, and QANTIS workflow analysis.

map.name: shanghai-map.case
map.title: Quality of Life in Shanghai
map.copy: Led an eight-person mixed-methods study of older Shanghai neighborhoods. Built an interactive map around nearby services and walking time, then helped translate the findings into community information campaigns.

details.label: FIELD RESEARCH
details.copy: Questionnaires and interviews informed the project. In the early 48-person presentation sample, respondents reported 6.75 / 10 average familiarity with nearby stores and amenities.

details.label: INTERACTIVE MAP
details.copy: Built a fixed-map interface in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with facility categories, 5-, 10-, and 15-minute filters, and an early place-detail interaction.

details.label: COMMUNITY ACTION
details.copy: Organized food-safety and anti-fraud information campaigns for older residents alongside the digital intervention.

details.label: EVIDENCE LIMIT
details.copy: The map was a prototype designed around the research findings. It was not formally user-tested, and no long-term quality-of-life outcome was measured.

allocation.name: course-allocation.py
allocation.title: Automatic and Satisfactory Course Assignment
allocation.copy: Built a Python and NumPy assignment pipeline for capacity-constrained courses, treating automation, efficiency, fairness, and preference satisfaction as separate design criteria.

details.label: MECHANISM
details.copy: Modeled ranked preferences and course capacity, generated a fractional allocation with Simultaneous Eating, then used Birkhoff decomposition to produce assignments that could be issued.

details.label: ITERATION
details.copy: Version 2 balanced remaining course capacity against remaining student capacity instead of distributing residual probability through random leftover courses.

details.label: REPORTED RESULT
details.copy: The original presentation reported that maximum-weight realization placed about 70% of students in a top-two choice and 92% in a top-three choice across 1,000 simulations.

details.label: TRANSFER
details.copy: Extended the allocation framework to parent–teacher meeting time slots by adapting the scoring logic to a second scheduling context.

emg.name: emg-monitor.device
emg.title: Monitoring Device for Muscle Usage & Behavior
emg.copy: An embedded prototype designed to make target-muscle recruitment observable during exercise, rather than only displaying a raw waveform.

details.label: DESIGN DECISION
details.copy: Compared EMG with angular-displacement sensing, then selected EMG because subtle target-muscle contraction was not reliably visible through changes in skin geometry.

details.label: CURRENT CHAIN
details.copy: The firmware filters and squares the signal, applies Kalman filtering, calibrates an individual reference, classifies four relative bands, and reports session percentages.

details.label: PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
details.copy: Designed the enclosure and internal packaging in Fusion and AutoCAD. The current STEP artifact contains one solid body with source bounds of approximately 30.79 × 58.00 × 10.00.

details.label: CURRENT LIMIT
details.copy: The current system produces a relative-activation distribution. The visualization, adaptive calibration, and exercise-interpretation layers remain in development.

research.title: How does agreement on principles affect perceived relevance?
research.copy: Transforming ethical-case survey responses into a shared quantitative representation while preserving the metadata needed for later analysis.
research.quote: STATUS: THE BROADER SIMILARITY–RELEVANCE QUESTION REMAINS OPEN.

details.label: TRANSFORMATION
details.copy: Parsed comma-separated principle labels, counted occurrences, normalized each count by the row total, and constructed ordered principle vectors.

details.label: TOOL DIVISION
details.copy: Used Python and pandas for transformation, Google Sheets for subsequent formulas, and R for regression analysis shared with the team.

details.label: CURRENT RESULT
details.copy: Current linear models did not find a relationship between principle frequency and agreement for the principles examined.

details.label: CONTRIBUTION
details.copy: Contributed data transformation and empirical analysis; the lab's ethical-principle taxonomy was not my authorship.

internship.title: Software Engineering Internship
internship.copy: Responsibilities span laboratory automation, localized scientific-software validation, workflow analysis for interface design, and technical enablement for team onboarding.
internship.quote: YOLO26 / ROS2 / AGENTIC ENGINEERING / SOFTWARE TESTING

details.label: LABORATORY AUTOMATION
details.copy: Built the perception layer for automated laboratory tube handling with YOLO26-based object detection. Connected detection output to ROS2 robot-arm workflows for tube grasping and placement.

details.label: F1 / 3500Dx
details.copy: Executed black-box dynamic workflow test cases for F1 on the 3500Dx instrument. Clarified expected behavior and product workflows when test cases required additional context.

details.label: QANTIS
details.copy: Analyzed WinTrace, the previous EDXRF software. Documented page transitions and interaction paths in Miro to support the redesign.

details.label: INTERN ONBOARDING
details.copy: Onboarded a new intern to the testing environment. Set up the virtual machine, provided software training, resolved setup issues, and supported the transition to independent testing.
